## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from Springer publisher pages and domain knowledge of accessibility research editorial culture (ACM SIGACCESS overlap, accessibility / inclusive design community). Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Very High |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **universal access / inclusion contribution**.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Pure HCI without accessibility focus redirected.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Pure HCI without accessibility focus
- AI use without disclosure per Springer policy

### Soft Tax

Low for accessibility tradition.

### Best Suited For

- Accessibility research
- Assistive technology
- Aging × technology
- Inclusive / universal design
- Disability HCI
- Participatory design with disability communities

### Not Recommended For

- Pure HCI (consider TOCHI)
- Pure engineering (consider IEEE)

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [ACM Transactions on Accessible Computing](../hci/acm-transactions-on-accessible-computing.md) | ACM SIGACCESS flagship |
| 2 | [International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction](../hci/international-journal-of-human-computer-interaction.md) | Broader applied HCI |
| 3 | [ACM Transactions on Computer-Human Interaction](../hci/acm-transactions-on-computer-human-interaction.md) | ACM SIGCHI |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from TOCHI as "too accessibility-specialized," UAIS is the Springer accessibility community home.
